articles.title: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
articles.summary: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Nvidia, Jensen Huang olayını araştırması için New York'un önde gelen hukuk firmasını işe aldı
articles.summaryTr: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
articles.articleText: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affir between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy. Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation" into the affair. The FBI is also conducting its own probe. The firm's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (£375bn) being wiped of its stock market value since Friday. Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom given it is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for successfully operating AI tools. It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials keen to win the AI race. Alice Huang was an executive at a Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia. The company had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked. Nvidia has also maintained the US government did not inform the firm that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern. According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring of this year warning that the Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected claims that Jensen Huang has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China". US President Donald Trump said Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang and that the Nvidia boss told him "I had no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed the him. However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Jensen Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing. The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. The committee has the authority to subpoena Jensen Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before the committee, if deemed necessary. When announcing on Sunday that it would investigate the affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe. - What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published1 hour ago Joon Kim, who will lead Nvidia's investigation, is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focused on fraud and other criminal acts. Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce. The investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with Nvidia. He has become a key public figure in the development on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity. It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang. A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any additional of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI. - Published14 hours ago

articles.titleTr: ABD'de Nvidia krizi siyasete sıçradı! Trump'a 'ulusal güvenliği tehlikeye attı' suçlaması
articles.summaryTr: ABD Senatosu Demokrat Lideri Schumer, Trump'ı Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkındaki casusluk iddialarına rağmen harekete geçmemekle suçladı. Kongre'de şirketin Çin'e çip satışları ve ulusal güvenlik bağlantılı faaliyetleri mercek altında.
articles.articleText: ABD'de Nvidia krizi siyasete sıçradı! Trump'a 'ulusal güvenliği tehlikeye attı' suçlaması - ABD Senatosu Demokrat Lideri Schumer, Trump'ı Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkındaki casusluk iddialarına rağmen harekete geçmemekle suçladı. Kongre'de şirketin Çin'e çip satışları ve ulusal güvenlik bağlantılı faaliyetleri mercek altında. ABD Senatosu Demokrat Azınlık Lideri Chuck Schumer, Başkan Donald Trump'ı Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkındaki casusluk bağlantılı iddialara rağmen şirket yöneticisini savunmakla suçladı. Schumer, Trump'ın ulusal güvenlik yerine Huang'ın çıkarlarını koruduğunu öne sürerken, Kongre'de Nvidia hakkında kapsamlı soruşturma çağrıları giderek artıyor. Schumer: Trump, Çinli casus iddialarına rağmen harekete geçmedi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle New York Times'ın haberlerine göre Trump'a, Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu öne sürülen Megaspeed yöneticisi Alice Huang ile ilişkisi hakkında bir yıldan uzun süre önce bilgi verildi. Schumer, Senato kürsüsünde yaptığı konuşmada Trump'ın bu bilgilere rağmen herhangi bir adım atmadığını savundu. Schumer, "Ulusal güvenlik açısından en önemli şirketlerimizden birinin CEO'sunun Çinli bir casusla ilişkisi olabileceği konuşuluyor ve Trump bu konuda hiçbir şey yapmadı" ifadelerini kullandı. Trump ise pazartesi günü yaptığı açıklamada iddiaları kısa süre önce öğrendiğini ima etmiş ve Jensen Huang'ın Alice Huang'ın casus olduğundan haberi bulunmadığı yönündeki açıklamasına inandığını söylemişti. Nvidia'nın Çin politikası da tartışmanın merkezinde Schumer, Trump'ın bu yılın başlarında Huang'ı Pekin'e gerçekleştirdiği devlet ziyaretine davet ettiğini ve Nvidia CEO'sunun tavsiyesini dikkate alarak Çin'in bazı gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine erişimine izin verdiğini öne sürdü. Demokrat lider ayrıca Nvidia'nın Trump'ın tartışmalı Beyaz Saray balo salonu projesine 25 milyon dolar bağış yaptığını hatırlattı. Schumer, ABD'nin en gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerinin potansiyel rakip ülkelerin eline geçmemesi gerektiğini belirterek, ihracat kısıtlamalarının gevşetilmesinde Nvidia'nın etkisinin araştırılmasını istedi. Cumhuriyetçiler de Huang'dan açıklama bekliyor Temsilciler Meclisi Çin Komitesi Başkanı Cumhuriyetçi John Moolenaar da Jensen Huang'ın Alice Huang ile ilişkisine ilişkin kapsamlı bir şirket içi soruşturma yürütülmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Moolenaar, Huang'ın Çinli bir istihbarat görevlisiyle hassas bilgiler paylaşıp paylaşmadığının, Çin'e çip satışlarının engellenmesine karşı lobi faaliyetlerinde etkilenip etkilenmediğinin ve Çinli şirketlere Nvidia'nın sınırlı sayıdaki gelişmiş çiplerinin satın alınmasında öncelik tanınıp tanınmadığının açıklığa kavuşturulmasını istedi. Moolenaar, soruşturmanın yalnızca bir hasar kontrolü çalışmasına dönüşmesi halinde kamuoyunun güveninin sağlanamayacağını ifade etti. Cumhuriyetçi Temsilci Brian Mast da Huang'a yöneltilecek sorular arasında Nvidia çiplerinin hangi şirketlere satıldığı, Megaspeed'in bu çipleri hangi amaçla kullandığı ve Nvidia donanımlarına uzaktan kimlerin eriştiği konularının bulunduğunu belirtti. Kongre'de soruşturma baskısı artıyor Huang'ın Kongre'ye bilgi vermesi talebi, her iki partiden milletvekillerinin desteğini alıyor. Cumhuriyetçi Brian Mast, John Moolenaar ve Rick Crawford, 5 Kasım'da Huang'a ortak bir mektup göndererek Çin Komitesi, Temsilciler Meclisi Dış İlişkiler Komitesi ve İstihbarat Komitesi'ne bilgi vermesini istemişti. Demokratların ocak ayında Temsilciler Meclisi ve Senato'da çoğunluğu devralmasıyla Nvidia ve Huang hakkındaki incelemelerin daha da genişlemesi bekleniyor. Schumer ayrıca Çin'in gelişmiş Amerikan teknolojilerine erişimini sınırlandırmayı amaçlayan AI OVERWATCH Act, MATCH Act ve Chip Security Act adlı yasa tasarılarının geçirilmesi için Cumhuriyetçilere çağrıda bulundu. Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu'nun da Huang hakkındaki iddialar ve şirket sırları ile ulusal güvenliğin tehlikeye girip girmediği konusunda bağımsız soruşturma başlattığı açıklanmıştı.

articles.summaryTr: The 82-year-old was placed under house detention in Florida last week after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
articles.articleText: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor - Published Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents. Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning. US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show. Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device. The BBC has contacted his representatives. Griffin described Markle's housing situation as "untenable", writing in the order revoking his pretrial release that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court". He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician". "Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday. "We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," he added. Markle, 82, was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said. Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material. Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material. In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old. Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention. He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ. FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions". Markle has called the allegations "sick lies". He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated. The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls. In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed." She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children". articles.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
articles.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, hotter-than-expected US inflation raised concerns about a larger Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December, Coinbase and Kalshi joined four other firms backing the CFTC in a lawsuit over single-stock perpetual futures, and cybersecurity firm CertiK urged crypto exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings. Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December Crypto industry experts warned on Tuesday that higher-than-expected US inflation could lead to a another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, making borrowing more expensive and potentially discouraging investment in cryptocurrencies. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% month over month in October, above economists’ forecast of 0.3%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics - a slower increase than September’s 0.6% rise. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, above the expected 0.2%. Currently, the Federal Reserve holds its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, after raising it by a quarter-point in September and leaving it unchanged in October. The report came just a few hours after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in London that another core inflation reading of 0.3% or higher could prompt the Fed to consider a larger interest rate hike in December. “In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25-basis-points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said.

articles.summaryTr: A majority of 49 to 24 assembly members backed the legislation, which was proposed by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker and welcomed by some parents and charities.
articles.articleText: Law on 'holiday hunger' passed by Stormont assembly - Published A law aimed at helping lower income families with food costs during school holidays has been passed by the Northern Ireland Assembly. The Holiday Meal Payments Bill seeks to create a new payment for families whose children receive free school meals to help with food costs outside of term time. A majority of 49 to 24 assembly members backed the legislation, which was proposed by Sinn Féin's Danny Baker and welcomed by some parents and charities. Education Minister Paul Givan described the bill as "fiscally reckless", warning it would cost £20m to £30m a year and lead to cuts elsewhere within his Stormont department. Baker said that "poverty isn't green and orange" and the passage of the bill would support thousands of children "across all of our communities". "When children are returning to school hungry, then they're not learning," he told assembly members during the bill's final stage debate. "If you want to deal with educational underachievement then you have to deal with poverty." Givan described the bill as "well intentioned" but said "sincerity is not a funding model". The Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) minister added there was "no such thing as a free lunch" and the legislation "will require cuts to be made" to other services. "So I ask those who support this bill, what cuts should be made to afford this payment?" The minister argued efforts at Stormont to tackle poverty should be made "in a coordinated way" across the entire four-party executive. Last month, Givan's department tabled amendments that would have given him power to delay its implementation, but these were rejected by a majority of parties. Funding for bill 'relatively small' Stormont assembly members voted on the bill on Tuesday night after more than four hours of debate during its final stage in the chamber. Alliance Party assembly member Nick Mathison, chair of the assembly's education committee, said "holiday hunger" remained a significant issue for many families. He acknowledged Stormont's financial pressures but said the funding required for the bill was a "relatively small" proportion of the Department of Education's budget. "When we are in a budgetary crisis we need to be ensuring that we do not end up penalising those who are least able to bear the costs," he added. Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) leader Jon Burrows commended Baker on the sentiment of his private member's bill but warned "there is no funding stream and there is no money". He said the bill "lacks any governance", adding: "There are no guarantees the money given under this will end up in nutritious meals inside the stomachs of children." "It's a fundamental misapplication and misunderstanding of how the welfare system should work," he told assembly members. Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) assembly member Cara Hunter welcomed the bill, saying that "a child can't learn on an empty stomach". "Hunger shows up in concentration, in behaviour and attainment long before it shows up in the spreadsheets or the speeches that we have before us here today," she added. Why was the bill introduced? Baker said he was motivated to introduce it by some of his experiences of breakfast clubs and meal schemes in youth work. "There was a young boy, about the same age of my youngest, around seven years old," he explained. "He was filling his wee pockets up and we caught on to this. "To cut a long story short, he was bringing home food for his siblings because there just wasn't enough food in the house." Baker said all ministers had choices to make and the legislation alone could not solve child poverty, but would act as an "early intervention". Children are eligible for free school meals if their family's household income is below £15,390 a year. Northern Ireland is the only UK region without government-funded holiday food support, after the Department of Education (DE) ended its £27-per-fortnight holiday meal grant in 2023. Baker's legislation was introduced in the Northern Ireland Assembly in March and has been scrutinised by members of the legislative assembly (MLAs) on a number of occasions over the past nine months. What have campaigners and charities said? Community and voluntary groups have been publicly supportive of the bill, with some staging a demonstration at Stormont on Monday in a bid to urge MLAs to get it over the finish line. Louise McCullough, a mum-of-three from east Belfast, was among those who spoke at the event. She said her children receive free school meals and that she would be directly affected by the legislation. "There are so many working families who need this, it will change their lives and be massively impactful," she told BBC News NI. "I can't afford to work full time because of the cost of childcare, and the cost of living. "We have to do what we can and schemes like free school meals make a difference but so much more needs done... if you can't find money for hungry children what are you doing? "Our government should be scaffolding our families properly." Edel Diamond from the South West Belfast Foodbank said organisations like hers had been "filling in the gaps" to help struggling families. "We shouldn't have to - it's incumbent on our executive to put these initiatives forward," she said. "This will make such a difference to families we're seeing daily." - Published30 March 2023 - Published12 October

articles.title: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.summary: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
articles.summaryTr: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
articles.articleText: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair. It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company. Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters. Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair? US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked. However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking". It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment. When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not. "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC. China has rejected the spying allegations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." The New York Times reported in late October that US President Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf. Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's [Jensen Huang] an honourable guy." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang. Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Jensen Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman. - Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published14 hours ago - Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published44 minutes ago Why does it matter? Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers. Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities. The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security. This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way. Sunday's revelations may explain why Jensen Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China. Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. Jensen Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic and perfectionist with incredibly high standards for his staff. He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?'" "He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. What investigations are now under way? Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into the affair and has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry out the probe. The investigation will be led by former US Attorney for New York's Southern District, Joon Kim. US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also investigating the affair. The FBI declined to comment further when contacted by the BBC. Jensen Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November. Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked the Nvidia chief executive to appear to explain his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage. Jensen Huang has yet to say he will comply, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. What is Nvidia and how important is it? Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates. Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch. "Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them," Witt told the BBC. Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure, including Amazon, Meta, Google, and Microsoft, now use Nvidia chips. Currently worth about $4tn, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world. For now, the firm's board appears to have little appetite for removing Jensen Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team". Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy. His children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at Nvidia in senior roles. Who is Jensen Huang's wife? Jensen Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners. They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer. In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn. Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University. Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him". "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad." Additional reporting by Tom McArthur in London, Ayeshea Perera and Tessa Wong in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney - Published21 September

articles.titleTr: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
articles.summaryTr: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
articles.articleText: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says - Published The first of two days of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions, President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was not at the talks, said they had proved "constructive and quite substantive". Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive". Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. Zelensky also said that humanitarian issues such as prisoner of war exchanges had been discussed. At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war". Kushner had said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. Asked later at a news conference in Copenhagen about the approach of US officials to negotiations, Zelensky said: "I see changes. I'm very happy with what I hear." Kushner and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting. Until now European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them. The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term". However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official. Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said. Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict. A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations". "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." articles.title: Why does Australia want Brits to swap Sydney for the outback?
articles.summary: Australia wants changes to UK deal that would push backpackers out of Bondi and into remote regions.

articles.titleTr: Why does Australia want Brits to swap Sydney for the outback?
articles.summaryTr: Australia wants changes to UK deal that would push backpackers out of Bondi and into remote regions.
articles.articleText: Why does Australia want Brits to swap Sydney for the outback? - Published In a Mexican restaurant in north-east Australia, the nacho bowls are served by staff from France, Italy, Ireland and Argentina. Cairns has long attracted a young and transient international crowd, who enjoy the tropical lifestyle while earning money for travel. But one nationality is in shorter supply than it used to be. "You get far fewer British backpackers looking for jobs here these days," says Mexicairns owner Peter McLeay. It's a trend McLeay has noticed since mid-2023, when a free trade deal between the UK and Australia kicked in. That agreement - as well as tariff-free trade in Tim Tams and Penguins - included special treatment for Brits on working holiday visas: exemption from having to find jobs in regional or remote places if they wanted to remain beyond a year. That, along with an increase in the age limit from 30 to 35 saw backpacker visas issued to Brits surging from 47,200 in 2023-24 to just over 77,000 in 2025-26, according to the latest Australian government data. Without the incentive to go regional, many are choosing to base themselves in the big cities, or, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, "Bondi or Coogee" - two of Sydney's most famous beachside suburbs. Now though, with Brits making up almost a quarter of all 323,000 backpacker visas issued last year, his government wants the free trade deal to be revisited. A privilege not enjoyed by others "Many Brits don't treat it as a working holiday anymore. It's more a three-year career break," says Dan McConnell, general manager of the Mad Monkey backpacker hostel chain. He says Brits used to be the largest clientele at its Cairns accommodation but "now French outnumber British three to one". "We see the Brits get to Sydney, decide it's the coolest place in the world, and stay there," he adds. It's a privilege not enjoyed by working holidaymakers from other countries who must do at least 88 days of "specified regional work" in industries that need a seasonal or temporary workforce - including agriculture, fisheries, tourism and hospitality - if they want to quality for a second year extension, and six months to stay a third year. Barely a month ago, Albanese ruled out forcing British backpackers to do the same, accepting it as part of the trade deal. But, under pressure from businesses here in Far North Queensland and other regional Australian communities, who are concerned about a lack of labour, the mood music has changed. Last week Albanese met UK counterpart Andy Burnham at the meeting of Commonwealth leaders in the Caribbean. And alongside AI, gender violence online and the AUKUS defence pact, backpackers were on the agenda. Despite speculation in the Australian media, no immediate announcement was made. Albanese instead told reporters that he had pushed for a change in the rules on backpackers and that Burnham had been "very constructive about it". "We'll work those issues through over coming weeks," he said adding that the free trade agreement was not set in stone and tweaks could be made "if there are good policy reasons". Backpackers make up one in seven farm jobs across Australia, with about 52,000 people on working holiday visas doing jobs in horticulture each year, according to the National Farmers Federation. It welcomed Albanese's discussions with Burnham, but said the issue of worker shortages in agriculture was far broader than the UK deal. Of greater concern are wider proposals, announced in September, to cut net migration into Australia, under political pressure from the resurgent right wing populist One Nation party and the opposition coalition. That includes an overhaul of the working holiday visa system, introducing a ballot for backpackers wanting to extend their stay – capped at 45,000 for people wanting a second year in Australia (down from 57,000 who qualified this year) and just 5,000 allowed to remain for a third year (compared with 31,000 this year). This, the federation says, is "a low blow". Those plans are still out for consultation, but immigration officials have slowed processing rates for some working holiday visa applications and paused them from several countries. Tourism Tropical North Queensland chief executive Mark Olsen has also been among those lobbying Albanese in Canberra - telling him that backpackers brought both the spending power and the temporary labour needed to fill seasonal roles in a region famed as a gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and the Unesco world heritage listed Daintree rainforest. Young Brits temporarily living and working in this region peaked at around 20,000 he says. Now it's closer to 11,000. "Numbers have dropped significantly since the UK free trade agreement kicked in when border arrangements returned to normal [after the pandemic] in 2023 ," he said. A two-way street Cairns restaurateur Fintan Rafferty says that of about 180 staff on his payroll across four venues, only five are British. Prior to the visa rule change, that was closer to 25. UK workers came with good skills in hospitality and "were willing to work, and to work flexible hours", he told the BBC. And, he said, it was a two-way street. "The pay is very good, the conditions are very good. And one of the great things about the 88-days rule is that it forces people to travel. It's enriching their experience." Bucking the trend, at the bar of Gilligan's backpackers, Paige Tomlinson serves vodka and soda with plenty of ice and a broad South Yorkshire accent. The 27-year-old, from Barnsley, has been in Cairns for four months, attracted by the "chilled" lifestyle and local waterfalls. "Most people prefer Sydney and they question me all the time why I'm here," she laughs. "But I got to Sydney and I just didn't like it. It was too busy, too much like London and I don't like London." She says she'd like to see the regional work requirement brought in for all Brits, "getting them out their comfort zone". "If every other country's got to do it, why should we not?" About 200km north, at Red Valley Farm in Lakeland, general manger Peter Inderbitzen agrees. Workers mainly from Tonga, hired on a Pacific labour scheme, pick bananas there year-round, But Inderbitzen also relies heavily on backpackers, especially at peak avocado season, employing about 25 people for a couple of months each year. "It's very short, sharp, get it done, get it out kind of work," he told the BBC. "But without those pickers, the avos stay on the tree." While a few British backpackers were still applying for work, numbers had "completely dropped off" since the rule change, said Inderbitzen, who'd "love" to see British travellers having an incentive to head to the regions. "As much as it wasn't perfect, [that programme] was working." Back in Cairns, most of the young Brits the BBC tracks down are on tourist visas - but many want to return for a working holiday. Among them is Ethan Phillips, 23, from Buckinghamshire who has been having way too much fun to keep up to date with what politicians have been discussing. "It makes sense for them to want us to do [regional work] again," he says. "I mean I'd rather not do it, but if we have to, it's only three months … it can't be that bad."

articles.summary: TCMB, Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme iznini iptal etti. 10 Kasım tarihli karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı.

articles.summaryTr: TCMB, Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme iznini iptal etti. 10 Kasım tarihli karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı.
articles.articleText: Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı: Ozan Elektronik Para'nın faaliyet izni kaldırıldı YAYIN TARİHİ, 11 Kasım 2026 00:15 PAYLAŞ - TCMB, Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme iznini iptal etti. 10 Kasım tarihli karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı. Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB), Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme iznini iptal etti. Karar, 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı. Faaliyet izni iptal edildi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle TCMB'nin 10 Kasım 2026 tarihli ve 12111/21710 sayılı kararıyla Ozan Elektronik Para AŞ'nin faaliyet izninin iptal edilmesine karar verildi. Şirkete, 6 Eylül 2019 tarihli ve 8538 sayılı Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurulu kararıyla, 6493 sayılı Kanun kapsamında elektronik para kuruluşu olarak faaliyet gösterme izni verilmişti. İptal kararının dayanağı Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan kararda, faaliyet izninin 6493 sayılı Kanun'un 16'ncı maddesinin birinci fıkrasının (c) ve (e) bentleri, 19'uncu maddesi ve 21'inci maddesinin sekizinci fıkrası uyarınca iptal edildiği belirtildi.

articles.articleText: Güney Kore'den ithal protez diş parçalarına damping! Kilogram başına 320 dolar uygulanacak - Ticaret Bakanlığı, Güney Kore menşeli protez diş bağlantı parçalarının ithalatında damping önlemlerini güncelledi. Bazı firmalara yüzde 15, bazılarına kilogram başına 140 veya 320 dolar, diğer firmalara ise yüzde 25 önlem uygulanacak. Ticaret Bakanlığı, Güney Kore menşeli protez dişlerin bağlantı parçalarının ithalatında uygulanan dampinge karşı önlemleri güncelledi. Yeni düzenlemeyle bazı üreticiler için yüzde 15 oranındaki önlem korunurken, bazı firmalara kilogram başına 140 ve 320 dolar tutarında önlem getirildi. Bazı üreticilere kilogram başına 320 dolar önlem CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 11 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan tebliğle, 2025/4 sayılı İthalatta Haksız Rekabetin Önlenmesine İlişkin Tebliğ'in ilgili maddesindeki tablo değiştirildi. 9021.29.00.00.00 GTİP numaralı, protez dişlerin bağlantı parçalarını kapsayan ürünlerde Güney Kore menşeli ithalata yönelik dampinge karşı önlemler firma bazında yeniden düzenlendi. Düzenlemeye göre Dio Corporation için kilogram başına 140 dolar, Evidence Implant Inc. ve Megagen Implant Co. Ltd. için kilogram başına 320 dolar önlem uygulanacak. Diğer firmalar için yüzde 15 ve yüzde 25 oranları ACH Medical, Biotem, Cowellmedi, Dentis, Dentium, KJ Meditech, Neobiotech ve Osstem Implant şirketleri için CIF bedelinin yüzde 15'i oranında dampinge karşı önlem belirlendi. Listede yer almayan diğer firmalar için ise CIF bedelinin yüzde 25'i oranında önlem uygulanacak. Tebliğ, yayımlandığı tarihte yürürlüğe girecek ve hükümlerini Ticaret Bakanı yürütecek.

articles.titleTr: İspanya'dan TikTok'a sert talep: Çocuk istismarı bitene kadar faaliyetleri durdurun!
articles.summaryTr: İspanya, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarı içeren videoların 48 milyon kez izlendiğini ortaya koyan araştırmanın ardından platformdan içerikler kaldırılana kadar ülkedeki faaliyetlerini askıya almasını istedi.
articles.articleText: İspanya'dan TikTok'a sert talep: Çocuk istismarı bitene kadar faaliyetleri durdurun! - İspanya, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarı içeren videoların 48 milyon kez izlendiğini ortaya koyan araştırmanın ardından platformdan içerikler kaldırılana kadar ülkedeki faaliyetlerini askıya almasını istedi. İspanya hükümeti, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarı içeren videoların en az 48 milyon kez izlendiğini ortaya koyan araştırmanın ardından platformdan ülkedeki faaliyetlerini askıya almasını istedi. Gençlik Bakanlığı, konuyla ilgili savcılığa ve Veri Koruma Ajansı'na başvurdu. 1.183 paylaşım belgelendi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İspanyol doğrulama kuruluşu Maldita.es'in yayımladığı araştırmada, TikTok'ta çocuk cinsel istismarını açıkça gösteren videoların en az 48 milyon kez görüntülendiği tespit edildi. Araştırmada toplam 1.183 müstehcen paylaşım belgelendi. Ayrıca 26 binden fazla profilin söz konusu içeriklere yorum yaptığı veya bu paylaşımları yeniden dolaşıma soktuğu belirtildi. İspanya hükümeti savcılığa başvurdu Gençlik Bakanlığı'nın açıklamasına göre, TikTok'u İspanya'da tek başına yasaklama yetkisi bulunmayan Gençlik Bakanı Sira Rego, platforma karşı adım atılması için savcılığa ve Veri Koruma Ajansı'na başvurdu. Rego, konuya ilişkin açıklamasında, "Sosyal medya hukuksuz bir alan olamaz" dedi. Talep, Başbakan Pedro Sanchez hükümetinin yapay zekayla üretilen çocuk cinsel istismarı içeriklerini yaydıkları iddiasıyla X, Meta ve TikTok hakkında soruşturma açılmasını istemesinden aylar sonra geldi. TikTok bazı arama terimlerini kısıtladı Maldita.es, salı akşamı yayımladığı yeni haberde TikTok'un araştırmada çocuk istismarı içeriklerine erişim sağladığı belirlenen iki arama terimini İspanya'daki kullanıcılar için kısıtladığını bildirdi. Ancak kuruluş, diğer Avrupa ülkelerinden yapılan aramaların hâlâ aynı içeriklere ulaşılmasını sağladığını belirtti.

articles.titleTr: Fed piyasaları sarstı: ABD'de 10 yıllık tahvil faizi yeniden yüzde 5'e dayandı!
articles.summaryTr: ABD'de ekim enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'den gelen şahin mesajlar tahvil faizlerini yükseltti. 10 yıllık tahvil getirisi yüzde 5'e ulaşırken, aralık ayında faiz artırımı beklentileri güçlendi.
articles.articleText: Fed piyasaları sarstı: ABD'de 10 yıllık tahvil faizi yeniden yüzde 5'e dayandı! - ABD'de ekim enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed'den gelen şahin mesajlar tahvil faizlerini yükseltti. 10 yıllık tahvil getirisi yüzde 5'e ulaşırken, aralık ayında faiz artırımı beklentileri güçlendi. ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentileri aşması ve Fed yetkilisi Christopher Waller'ın sert faiz artışı mesajı vermesi, tahvil piyasasında satışları hızlandırdı. 10 yıllık ABD Hazine tahvilinin getirisi yüzde 5'e yükselirken, aralık ayında faiz artırımı beklentileri güçlendi. 10 yıllık tahvil faizi yüzde 5 seviyesine çıktı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ABD Hazine tahvillerinde getiriler salı günü yükseldi. Gösterge niteliğindeki 10 yıllık tahvilin faizi 14 baz puan artışla yüzde 5'e ulaştı. 30 yıllık tahvilin getirisi 11 baz puandan fazla yükselerek yüzde 5,37'ye, Fed'in kısa vadeli faiz beklentilerini yakından izleyen 2 yıllık tahvilin getirisi ise 19 baz puan artışla yüzde 4,738'e çıktı. 10 yıllık tahvil faizi, bu ayın başlarında da yüzde 5 seviyesinin üzerinde işlem görmüştü. Ekim ayında 10 ve 30 yıllık tahvil getirileri 24 yılın en yüksek seviyelerine ulaşmıştı. Tahvil piyasasındaki satışları, 42 milyar dolarlık 10 yıllık tahvil ihalesine gelen görece zayıf talep de hızlandırdı. İhale sonrasında tahvil getirileri bir miktar daha yükseldi. ABD enflasyonu beklentileri aştı ABD'de tüketici fiyat endeksi (TÜFE) ekim ayında aylık yüzde 0,4 arttı. Ekonomistlerin beklentisi yüzde 0,3 seviyesindeydi. Eylül ayında aylık enflasyon yüzde 0,6 olarak açıklanmıştı. Gıda ve enerji fiyatlarının hariç tutulduğu çekirdek TÜFE ise aylık yüzde 0,3 yükseldi. Piyasa beklentisi yüzde 0,2 artış yönündeydi. Çekirdek enflasyon eylül ayında da yüzde 0,3 artmıştı. Waller'dan 50 baz puanlık faiz artışı mesajı Fed Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Christopher Waller, enflasyon verilerinin beklentilerin üzerinde gelmesi durumunda daha güçlü adımlar atılması gerektiğini söyledi. İngiltere Merkez Bankası'nın ev sahipliğinde Londra'da düzenlenen konferansta konuşan Waller, aralık ayındaki toplantıda 50 baz puanlık faiz artışının değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtti. Waller, yalnızca 25 baz puanlık artışın Fed'in güvenilirliğini riske atabileceğini ifade etti. Goldman Sachs Asset Management Çok Sektörlü Sabit Getirili Yatırımlar Başkanı Lindsay Rosner da yüksek enflasyonun Fed'in faiz artırımlarını 2027'ye taşıyabileceği uyarısında bulundu. Rosner, aralık ayında faiz artırımını temel beklentileri olarak gördüklerini ve 2027'de yeni artışların da ihtimal dahilinde olduğunu söyledi. Piyasalar aralık ayında faiz artırımını fiyatlıyor CME Group'un FedWatch aracına göre piyasalar, Fed'in aralık ayında 25 baz puanlık faiz artırımını büyük ölçüde fiyatlamış durumda. Geçen cuma açıklanan ve beklentilerin iki katından fazla gelen istihdam verisi de faiz artışı beklentilerini güçlendirmişti. Petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme ise enflasyon beklentileri açısından farklı bir görünüm oluşturdu. Brent petrolün varil fiyatı, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın İran'la savaşın yakında sona erebileceğine ilişkin açıklamalarının ardından salı sabahı ağustos ayından bu yana ilk kez 90 doların altına indi. Gösterge niteliğindeki 10 yıllık tahvilin faizi 14 baz puan artışla yüzde 5'e ulaştı. 30 yıllık tahvilin getirisi 11 baz puandan fazla yükselerek yüzde 5,37'ye, Fed'in kısa vadeli faiz beklentilerini yakından izleyen 2 yıllık tahvilin getirisi ise 19 baz puan artışla yüzde 4,738'e çıktı. 10 yıllık tahvil faizi, bu ayın başlarında da yüzde 5 seviyesinin üzerinde işlem görmüştü. news.title: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair
news.summary: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.

news.titleTr: Nvidia, Jensen Huang olayını araştırması için New York'un önde gelen hukuk firmasını işe aldı
news.summaryTr: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
news.articleText: Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affir between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy. Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation" into the affair. The FBI is also conducting its own probe. The firm's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (£375bn) being wiped of its stock market value since Friday. Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom given it is the sole manufacturer of a crucial computer chip required for successfully operating AI tools. It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials keen to win the AI race. Alice Huang was an executive at a Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia. The company had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked. Nvidia has also maintained the US government did not inform the firm that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern. According to the New York Times, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington in spring of this year warning that the Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Beijing has rejected claims that Jensen Huang has been targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "intended to smear and malign China". US President Donald Trump said Monday that he had spoken to Jensen Huang and that the Nvidia boss told him "I had no idea she was a spy." Trump said he believed the him. However, the relationship has drawn more political attention. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs have asked Jensen Huang to appear next week for a closed door briefing. The Nvidia boss has yet to say whether he will attend, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. The committee has the authority to subpoena Jensen Huang, effectively forcing him to appear before the committee, if deemed necessary. When announcing on Sunday that it would investigate the affair, Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. It added that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe. - What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published1 hour ago Joon Kim, who will lead Nvidia's investigation, is a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District and spent several years working as a government attorney focused on fraud and other criminal acts. Wachtell is one of the largest law firms in the US and has several notable clients in the tech industry. Among them are OpenAI and Salesforce. The investigation will likely be treated as urgent, according to sources familiar with the matter, as Jensen Huang's public image is tightly intertwined with Nvidia. He has become a key public figure in the development on AI, arguing the technology is a "new industrial revolution" and is on par with the advent of electricity. It is unclear, however, if Wachtell will be able to interview Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang. A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment on Tuesday when asked if Jensen Huang had retained any additional of his own legal representation amid the company investigation and the separate one launched by the FBI. - Published14 hours ago

news.titleTr: ABD'de Nvidia krizi siyasete sıçradı! Trump'a 'ulusal güvenliği tehlikeye attı' suçlaması
news.summaryTr: ABD Senatosu Demokrat Lideri Schumer, Trump'ı Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkındaki casusluk iddialarına rağmen harekete geçmemekle suçladı. Kongre'de şirketin Çin'e çip satışları ve ulusal güvenlik bağlantılı faaliyetleri mercek altında.
news.articleText: ABD'de Nvidia krizi siyasete sıçradı! Trump'a 'ulusal güvenliği tehlikeye attı' suçlaması - ABD Senatosu Demokrat Lideri Schumer, Trump'ı Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkındaki casusluk iddialarına rağmen harekete geçmemekle suçladı. Kongre'de şirketin Çin'e çip satışları ve ulusal güvenlik bağlantılı faaliyetleri mercek altında. ABD Senatosu Demokrat Azınlık Lideri Chuck Schumer, Başkan Donald Trump'ı Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkındaki casusluk bağlantılı iddialara rağmen şirket yöneticisini savunmakla suçladı. Schumer, Trump'ın ulusal güvenlik yerine Huang'ın çıkarlarını koruduğunu öne sürerken, Kongre'de Nvidia hakkında kapsamlı soruşturma çağrıları giderek artıyor. Schumer: Trump, Çinli casus iddialarına rağmen harekete geçmedi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle New York Times'ın haberlerine göre Trump'a, Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu öne sürülen Megaspeed yöneticisi Alice Huang ile ilişkisi hakkında bir yıldan uzun süre önce bilgi verildi. Schumer, Senato kürsüsünde yaptığı konuşmada Trump'ın bu bilgilere rağmen herhangi bir adım atmadığını savundu. Schumer, "Ulusal güvenlik açısından en önemli şirketlerimizden birinin CEO'sunun Çinli bir casusla ilişkisi olabileceği konuşuluyor ve Trump bu konuda hiçbir şey yapmadı" ifadelerini kullandı. Trump ise pazartesi günü yaptığı açıklamada iddiaları kısa süre önce öğrendiğini ima etmiş ve Jensen Huang'ın Alice Huang'ın casus olduğundan haberi bulunmadığı yönündeki açıklamasına inandığını söylemişti. Nvidia'nın Çin politikası da tartışmanın merkezinde Schumer, Trump'ın bu yılın başlarında Huang'ı Pekin'e gerçekleştirdiği devlet ziyaretine davet ettiğini ve Nvidia CEO'sunun tavsiyesini dikkate alarak Çin'in bazı gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine erişimine izin verdiğini öne sürdü. Demokrat lider ayrıca Nvidia'nın Trump'ın tartışmalı Beyaz Saray balo salonu projesine 25 milyon dolar bağış yaptığını hatırlattı. Schumer, ABD'nin en gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerinin potansiyel rakip ülkelerin eline geçmemesi gerektiğini belirterek, ihracat kısıtlamalarının gevşetilmesinde Nvidia'nın etkisinin araştırılmasını istedi. Cumhuriyetçiler de Huang'dan açıklama bekliyor Temsilciler Meclisi Çin Komitesi Başkanı Cumhuriyetçi John Moolenaar da Jensen Huang'ın Alice Huang ile ilişkisine ilişkin kapsamlı bir şirket içi soruşturma yürütülmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Moolenaar, Huang'ın Çinli bir istihbarat görevlisiyle hassas bilgiler paylaşıp paylaşmadığının, Çin'e çip satışlarının engellenmesine karşı lobi faaliyetlerinde etkilenip etkilenmediğinin ve Çinli şirketlere Nvidia'nın sınırlı sayıdaki gelişmiş çiplerinin satın alınmasında öncelik tanınıp tanınmadığının açıklığa kavuşturulmasını istedi. Moolenaar, soruşturmanın yalnızca bir hasar kontrolü çalışmasına dönüşmesi halinde kamuoyunun güveninin sağlanamayacağını ifade etti. Cumhuriyetçi Temsilci Brian Mast da Huang'a yöneltilecek sorular arasında Nvidia çiplerinin hangi şirketlere satıldığı, Megaspeed'in bu çipleri hangi amaçla kullandığı ve Nvidia donanımlarına uzaktan kimlerin eriştiği konularının bulunduğunu belirtti. Kongre'de soruşturma baskısı artıyor Huang'ın Kongre'ye bilgi vermesi talebi, her iki partiden milletvekillerinin desteğini alıyor. Cumhuriyetçi Brian Mast, John Moolenaar ve Rick Crawford, 5 Kasım'da Huang'a ortak bir mektup göndererek Çin Komitesi, Temsilciler Meclisi Dış İlişkiler Komitesi ve İstihbarat Komitesi'ne bilgi vermesini istemişti. Demokratların ocak ayında Temsilciler Meclisi ve Senato'da çoğunluğu devralmasıyla Nvidia ve Huang hakkındaki incelemelerin daha da genişlemesi bekleniyor. Schumer ayrıca Çin'in gelişmiş Amerikan teknolojilerine erişimini sınırlandırmayı amaçlayan AI OVERWATCH Act, MATCH Act ve Chip Security Act adlı yasa tasarılarının geçirilmesi için Cumhuriyetçilere çağrıda bulundu. Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu'nun da Huang hakkındaki iddialar ve şirket sırları ile ulusal güvenliğin tehlikeye girip girmediği konusunda bağımsız soruşturma başlattığı açıklanmıştı.

news.articleText: Meghan's father Thomas Markle back in federal custody after allegedly removing ankle monitor - Published Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents. Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning. US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show. Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device. The BBC has contacted his representatives. Griffin described Markle's housing situation as "untenable", writing in the order revoking his pretrial release that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court". He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician". "Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday. "We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," he added. Markle, 82, was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said. Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material. Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material. In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old. Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention. He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ. FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions". Markle has called the allegations "sick lies". He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated. The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls. In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed." She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children". news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, hotter-than-expected US inflation raised concerns about a larger Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December, Coinbase and Kalshi joined four other firms backing the CFTC in a lawsuit over single-stock perpetual futures, and cybersecurity firm CertiK urged crypto exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings. Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December Crypto industry experts warned on Tuesday that higher-than-expected US inflation could lead to a another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, making borrowing more expensive and potentially discouraging investment in cryptocurrencies. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% month over month in October, above economists’ forecast of 0.3%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics - a slower increase than September’s 0.6% rise. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, above the expected 0.2%. Currently, the Federal Reserve holds its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, after raising it by a quarter-point in September and leaving it unchanged in October. The report came just a few hours after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in London that another core inflation reading of 0.3% or higher could prompt the Fed to consider a larger interest rate hike in December. “In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25-basis-points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said.
